name: Microsoft
whatIsRecord: Financial ledger, supply chain, customer records (Dynamics 365)
description: Dynamics 365 ERP/CRM — finance, supply chain, commerce, HR modules.
themes: agentic AI as platform shift ('one of the most consequential platform shifts')
AI monetization at scale ($37B ARR, 123% YoY; Copilot seats +250% YoY, 20M+ paid seats)
seats plus consumption pricing model (GitHub Copilot moves to usage-based)
Work IQ as system of record grounding layer (17 EB of org data, growing 35% YoY)
agent control plane (Agent 365: tens of millions of agents already managed)
agentic coding proliferation (GitHub Copilot enterprise subscribers tripled YoY)
summary: Microsoft continues to advance the most confident 'offensive' AI framing in enterprise software: management presents the current moment as a 'consequential platform shift' that expands every TAM rather than cannibalizes it. Satya Nadella frames the shift to a per-seat plus consumption model explicitly — GitHub Copilot converts to usage-based pricing this quarter — as evidence that AI is creating incremental monetization layers on top of the SaaS base. The 'Work IQ' data layer (17 EB and growing) is now positioned as the unmatched SoR grounding engine that makes Microsoft's agents structurally superior, reinforcing rather than undermining Microsoft's SaaS moat.

quotes.speaker: Satya Nadella
quotes.text: Our AI business surpassed $37 billion ARR, up 123%. We are at the beginning of one of the most consequential platform shifts that will change the entire tech stack as agents proliferate and become the dominant workload. This will drive TAM expansion and change the value creation equation across the entire economy.

quotes.speaker: Satya Nadella
quotes.text: In knowledge work, it was another record quarter for Microsoft 365 Copilot seat adds, which increased 250% year-over-year, representing our fastest growth since launch. Quarter-over-quarter, we continue to see acceleration and now have over 20 million Microsoft 365 Copilot paid seats.

quotes.speaker: Satya Nadella
quotes.text: The system of work behind Work IQ alone now spans more than 17 EB of data, growing 35% year-over-year. The liquidity and freshness of that data matters, with billions of emails, documents, chats, hundreds of millions of Teams meetings, and millions of SharePoint sites added each day. That context is getting even richer as Copilot adoption grows, Copilot and agent conversations and artifacts that create feedback into Work IQ, making it even more context rich.

quotes.speaker: Satya Nadella
quotes.text: Nearly 90% of the Fortune 500 now have active agents built with our low-code, no-code tools, and we are seeing fast growth of our Copilot credit consumptive offer, up nearly 2x quarter-over-quarter as customers increasingly extend Copilot with custom agents tailored to their workflows.

quotes.speaker: Satya Nadella
quotes.text: When it comes to biz apps, we are seeing a new pattern emerge as customers shift from traditional seat model to seats plus consumption. The customer service category is at the forefront of this transformation, as nearly 60% of our service customers are already purchasing usage-based credits.

quotes.speaker: Satya Nadella
quotes.text: Earlier this week, we announced our move to usage-based pricing model for GitHub Copilot as we align pricing to actual usage and costs.

quotes.speaker: Satya Nadella
quotes.text: Tens of thousands of companies are already managing tens of millions of agents in Agent 365, and we expect this momentum to grow significantly as agents will increasingly need tools for identity governance, security, and more.

quotes.speaker: Amy Hood
quotes.text: When I think about that model, I start to think about it as a license business plus a consumption business, and really applying far more broadly than I think people have thought about that. It starts to mean that over time bookings will actually also look a little different. It'll still have that per-seat license logic, but it'll also have a meter, just like you see in Azure.

name: Oracle
whatIsRecord: Financial ledger, supply chain, procurement, HR (Fusion + NetSuite)
description: Cloud ERP (Fusion Cloud, NetSuite). Dominant in enterprise and mid-market ERP.
themes: SaaSpocalypse narrative directly rebutted by name (Q3 continues Q1 pattern)
AI coding tools adopted internally (vibe coding accelerating SaaS development)
system of record defensibility (data gravity, mission-critical data, 2,000+ go-lives in Q3)
agentic AI strategy (1,000+ embedded agents in Fusion; autonomous book-close agent roadmap)
multi-cloud database as AI agent infrastructure ($553B RPO; 531% multi-cloud DB revenue growth YoY)
ecosystem automation play (healthcare, banking, retail end-to-end suites as competitive moat)
direct competitive attack on SAP and Workday by name (multiple win disclosures)
summary: Oracle maintained its combative 'offensive-defensive' stance in Q3 FY2026, with Mike Sicilia again naming and rejecting the 'SaaS apocalypse' and Larry Ellison framing Oracle as 'the disruptor' targeting entire industry ecosystems. The new emphasis this quarter is on ecosystem-scale automation — Oracle is building autonomous AI-agent suites that span entire verticals (healthcare, banking, retail) rather than individual applications, directly attacking Epic in healthcare and Salesforce/SAP in enterprise software by name with specific go-live wins. Larry Ellison added the autonomous financial close as a near-term product roadmap item, deepening the offensive narrative.

quotes.speaker: Mike Sicilia
quotes.text: In the context of that, I'll say a few words about the reported SaaS apocalypse. You've all heard the thesis or theory that new companies coding quickly using AI will spell the death of SaaS. I don't agree with that at all. I do think that AI tools and their coding capabilities would be a threat if we weren't adopting them, but we are, and very rapidly. Oracle is using the best AI coding tools and the best developers not only to accelerate our SaaS business, but to deliver solutions that enable entire ecosystems across numerous industries.

quotes.speaker: Mike Sicilia
quotes.text: We are building brand-new SaaS products using AI and also embedding AI agents right into our existing applications suites. By embracing AI with small engineering teams, we have just built three brand-new CX applications. Lead generation and qualification, sales orchestration, and automated selling, and our new website generator. These are three products that Salesforce.com does not have. Of course, Salesforce.com also doesn't have OCI, the AI data platform, Fusion ERP, and complete industry suites.

quotes.speaker: Mike Sicilia
quotes.text: We've already delivered well over 1,000 agents right inside our horizontal back office and industry applications. That banking suite alone contains hundreds of embedded AI agents, all available at no additional cost to our customers.

quotes.speaker: Mike Sicilia
quotes.text: In summary, these are not systems that can be replaced by a small collection of niche features cobbled together and bolted on in the name of AI. Yes, some smaller or single-focused SaaS players may well be disrupted, but Oracle will not be among them.

quotes.speaker: Larry Ellison
quotes.text: We plan in our Fusion accounting system, for example, we will have a complex agent that does something called the close. When you close your books with Fusion in the not too distant future, it will be an autonomous agent, no human beings involved. You will close your books by simply telling the AI agent to go ahead and close the books, and then you will get your results.

quotes.speaker: Larry Ellison
quotes.text: That's why we think we're a disruptor. That's why we think the SaaS apocalypse applies to others, but not to us.

quotes.speaker: Clay Magouyrk
quotes.text: The rapid improvement in model coding skills and agentic abilities pushes customers to move their most valuable data into our cloud services. They need access to the latest AI features to support vector embeddings, MCP server access, and advanced security controls. Customers also need their data to be co-located with the agents themselves, and our multi-cloud database makes that easy.

quotes.speaker: Mike Sicilia
quotes.text: The fact that we are the custodian in our applications business of so much of the world's mission-critical data, we have very close provisioning, very close proximity to these models. Putting those two things together allows customers to get value from AI very, very quickly.

name: SAP
whatIsRecord: Financial ledger, supply chain, manufacturing, procurement, HR
description: S/4HANA Cloud ERP — the backbone of global enterprise operations.
themes: SaaSpocalypse acknowledged with humility ('28% share price decline left its traces')
ERP as 'institutional brain' (50 years of domain knowledge, 7.3M data fields, 120 mission-critical processes)
honest AI limitations disclosed (agents '85%-90% accurate' — not enough for payroll/financial close at scale)
agentic AI strategy — 'All-in on AI' program (Joule, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot for 30%+ developer productivity)
Business Data Cloud as semantic integration layer (Reltio acquisition for master data governance)
consumption-based revenue shift (gradual transition; <40% of cloud revenue seat-based)
Sapphire 2026 as major announcement platform (fundamental architecture changes teased)
summary: SAP Q1 2026 is the most candid and self-critical call in this batch, with CEO Christian Klein explicitly acknowledging AI agent accuracy limitations ('85%-90% accurate is not enough for payroll and financial close') while simultaneously teasing fundamental architectural changes at Sapphire 2026. The tone is more 'defensive-offensive' than before: Klein leads with humility about the learning curve before asserting that SAP's 50-year domain knowledge and 7.3 million ERP data fields make them 'uniquely positioned' to solve the accuracy problem that no LLM provider can solve alone. CFO Dominik Asam even acknowledged the SaaSpocalypse debate directly caused a 28% share price decline.

quotes.speaker: Christian Klein
quotes.text: There is no doubt that AI will redefine how companies will run in the future. At the same time, let's be honest, large-scale adoption of enterprise AI is still in its early stages. Also, we at SAP are learning our lessons every day with our customers about what it really takes to make business AI work reliably, which is key when you run the world's most mission-critical and complex business processes.

quotes.speaker: Christian Klein
quotes.text: Agents often don't have yet the full understanding of business data and processes to deliver highly accurate outcomes. This is needed to deploy at scale and with high accuracy, agentic AI use cases in the most mission-critical parts of our customers' business.

quotes.speaker: Christian Klein
quotes.text: SAP's ERP, developed over 50 years, can also be seen as the institutional brain of every company, where data and process domain know-how is getting stored. The launch of SAP Business Data Cloud last year was another important step to enable our customers to further expand the SAP semantic data model to non-SAP data.

quotes.speaker: Christian Klein
quotes.text: We deliver those use cases, but today they are 85% accurate, they are 90% accurate. Is this enough when you are touching the payroll, the finance, the financial close, the supply chains of a customer? No, it's not enough. It's not that the customers don't see the value. They see the value, but we have to go the last mile.

quotes.speaker: Christian Klein
quotes.text: With Joule for ABAP development and by third-party tools like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot, we are increasing developer productivity already by over 30%. With AI assistance, our service and support teams are handling significantly higher ticket volumes without a proportional increase in headcount. AI assists 100% of support cases, and 20% of our tickets are even resolved by AI, fully autonomous.

quotes.speaker: Christian Klein
quotes.text: On the contrary, we expect to continue to gain market share with our best-of-suite offering, because now more than ever, a harmonized data and process layer is key to harnessing the power of AI. With the infusion of AI across our products and migration tools, you will see an increasing share of consumption-related cloud revenue in our P&L.

quotes.speaker: Dominik Asam
quotes.text: The SaaS apocalypse debate and the related 28% decline in our share price during the first quarter alone left its traces in that position. While we hedged the lion's share of our cash settled grants, the sheer magnitude of the move in the unhedged portion, in combination with related social charges that are not hedged, provided this, I have to admit, unintended relief.

quotes.speaker: Christian Klein
quotes.text: I don't believe that over these 7.3 million data fields and over 120 mission-critical business processes, I don't believe there's any other software company, for sure not the LLM providers, who actually can sort that out, and that's actually our task.

notes: SAP CFO explicitly mentioned the 'SaaS apocalypse debate' caused a 28% share price decline in Q1 2026, making this a rare earnings call where the disruption narrative had direct financial disclosure implications.

name: Salesforce
whatIsRecord: Customer accounts, contacts, opportunities, deals, cases
description: The dominant enterprise CRM system of record. Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Marketing Cloud.
themes: SaaSpocalypse mocked again ('not our first SaaSpocalypse', 'being eaten by the Sasquatch')
Agentforce as $800M business (29,000 deals in first 15 months, 50% QoQ growth)
agentic work units (AWU) — new metric (2.4 billion AWUs to date, 771M in Q4 alone)
platform hub play ('each agent phones home to Salesforce via MCP')
AI-driven large deals ($72B RPO, $50B repurchase — management confidence signal)
Data 360 as semantic layer ($2.9B ARR incl. Informatica, +200% YoY)
expansion via vertical disruption (ITSM vs. ServiceNow, Life Sciences vs. Veeva)
summary: Salesforce's Q4 FY2026 call is the most triumphant in this batch: Benioff named the SaaSpocalypse three times, dismissed it with bravado, and declared Agentforce an $800M business after 15 months. The stance has shifted from 'offensive-defensive' to pure 'offensive': there is virtually no defensive hedging — instead, management introduced the Agentic Work Unit (AWU) metric to quantify platform activity, declared a $50B buyback as a confidence signal, and announced vertical expansion directly attacking ServiceNow and Veeva by name. The 'phone home to Salesforce via MCP' hub thesis from Q1 is now quantified with 19 trillion tokens processed and 2.4B AWUs.

quotes.speaker: Marc Benioff
quotes.text: You know, this is not our first SaaSpocalypse. We have been through many SaaSpocalypses. You know, I remember the horrible SaaSpocalypse of 2020, when not only the software industry was dying, but we were all dying. We made it through that, and now everyone is back, doing great.

quotes.speaker: Marc Benioff
quotes.text: This level of financial performance is a clear signal that companies across every industry and region are investing in Salesforce to become agentic enterprises. Just like we've been talking about now for 2 years at Dreamforce, that the agentic enterprise is a real idea, and we're gonna talk about Agentforce, and I think it just became an $800 million business.

quotes.speaker: Marc Benioff
quotes.text: These agents can't work in isolation. You know, like ET, each one of them needs to phone home. That home is Salesforce, and they are calling us through the MCP server or maybe even just through one of our core platforms, and the more agents that our company deploys, us or anyone else, the more essential our platform becomes. This is my personal testimonial... if there is a SaaSpocalypse, I think it might be being eaten by the Sasquatch, because there are a lot of companies using a lot of SaaS, because SaaS just got a lot better with agents-as-a-service.

quotes.speaker: Marc Benioff
quotes.text: In its first 15 months, we closed 29,000 deals, up 50% year quarter-over-quarter. Customers in production have increased as well, nearly 50% in Q4.

quotes.speaker: Marc Benioff
quotes.text: Today, we are one of the largest consumers of tokens in the world to date, now over 19 trillion tokens. We continue to show you that because we want you to see that we're actually doing what we say. Another level is a token on its own doesn't know your customers, your pipeline, your org chart, but Salesforce does. The value isn't in the token. The value is when what our platform does with it, the work.

quotes.speaker: Marc Benioff
quotes.text: Today we're introducing an additional metric, the agentic work unit, created by our very own Patrick Stokes... An AWU represents one unit of AI work, agentic work unit. We're rolling this out to see how you like it, actually, here in earnings. It's a record updated, workflow triggered, decision made, MCP called. To date, AI agents on the Salesforce platform delivered 2.4 billion Agentic Work Units.

quotes.speaker: Marc Benioff
quotes.text: I especially loved 5 customers who got to leave the purgatory of ServiceNow, like Sunrun, Cornerstone, CoolSys, and there's others, too... We built an amazing new life sciences product this year, Agentforce for Life Sciences. Since we launched, so many of the global pharma companies... they're leaving Veeva... including AstraZeneca, Novartis, Takeda.

notes: CRM introduced the 'Agentic Work Unit' (AWU) as a new KPI this quarter. The $72B RPO and $50B buyback announcement are management's strongest possible confidence signal. Benioff explicitly named Anthropic's Dario Acemoglu and stated Salesforce invested $100M more into Anthropic this quarter.

name: Intuit
whatIsRecord: SMB financial ledger, tax records, payroll, invoicing
description: QuickBooks (the SMB accounting SoR), TurboTax, Mailchimp.
themes: system of record defensibility (regulated finance, 'category of one', high-liability moat)
'Service as a Software' rebranding (done-for-you vs. do-it-yourself positioning)
AI + HI combination as structural moat (human intelligence non-substitutable in high-stakes decisions)
AI-native ERP expansion (Intuit Enterprise Suite mid-market, construction edition launched)
LLM partnership strategy (Anthropic multi-year partnership; OpenAI app directory launch)
consumption-based monetization (payroll +, payments +29% volume, QB Live +50% YoY)
AI agent portfolio scaling (accounting, tax, finance, payments agents; 3M+ customers using agents)
summary: Intuit's Q2 FY2026 call deepens the 'defensive-offensive' positioning from Q1: CEO Sasan Goodarzi leads with the regulated, high-liability argument as a structural barrier to AI substitution, while announcing a major offensive move — a multiyear Anthropic partnership making Intuit the 'foundation' for AI agent builders in tax and financial domains. The AI + human intelligence (HI) combination is now quantified with operational metrics: accounting agents categorized 237M transactions in January alone, QB Live is up 50% YoY, and the business tax agent uncovers an average $1,000 in incremental deductions. The Intuit Enterprise Suite mid-market ERP push is the clearest new offensive vector.

quotes.speaker: Sasan Goodarzi
quotes.text: We are a category of one because our platform is mission-critical to our customers' financial lives. In our category, accuracy, compliance, security, reliability of financial decisions, and the liability that comes with it are critical to our customers. It's our advantage, and it's why we win.

quotes.speaker: Sasan Goodarzi
quotes.text: Earlier this month, we launched all four of our apps in OpenAI's app directory, and this week we announced a multiyear, game-changing partnership with Anthropic to advance highly personalized experiences for consumers and businesses. Powered by Intuit's decade of deep domain expertise and proprietary data models, the Intuit platform will become the foundation where businesses can build and customize secure, accurate, compliant AI agents.

quotes.speaker: Sasan Goodarzi
quotes.text: Zooming out, we're helping shape the future of financial intelligence by working with leading AI companies to meet consumers and businesses wherever they choose to work and get work done. These companies partner with Intuit because in a high-stakes, regulated environment where customers face significant liability if they get it wrong, they demand more than generic LLM recommendations.

quotes.speaker: Sasan Goodarzi
quotes.text: It's also the thing I would point out is it's why companies like OpenAI, companies like Anthropic, look to the partnership with us, because at the end of the day, they see and understand that this is a business that comes with a lot of liability, and LLMs can't just create the platform that we've created overnight.

quotes.speaker: Sasan Goodarzi
quotes.text: In our category of one, it's all about customer confidence in financial decisions, and the combination of data, AI, and human expertise is essential to success. That's why we have built a system of intelligence with APIs and MCP that spans a customer's financial life across their apps and data and is not confined to any one system.

quotes.speaker: Sasan Goodarzi
quotes.text: Our AI and HI capabilities are not only automating tasks and workflows, but driving consumption and adoption of services like payroll and powering QuickBooks Live customer growth of over 50% in Q2. In January alone, our accounting agents saved time and delivered impact for our customers by categorizing over 237 million transactions. This represents over half of all the transactions categorized that month.

quotes.speaker: Sandeep Aujla
quotes.text: The moat that we have comes from proprietary data. Sasan assured that that data is not leaving our four walls. Our moat comes from being the core of the flow of funds, whether it's access to capital, whether it's hours worked by the employees, whether it's the money flow, that's not being touched by these LLMs.

name: Shopify
whatIsRecord: Product catalog, orders, inventory, customer records for merchants
description: The SoR for millions of merchants — products, orders, inventory, customers.
themes: AI as 'native language' and 'exoskeleton' (forced AI adoption company-wide, every function)
commerce data moat compounding (20 years, billions of products, 1B+ structured products in catalog)
agentic commerce infrastructure play (UCP now joined by Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce, Stripe)
AI channel demand acceleration (AI-driven traffic 8x YoY; AI-powered orders 13x YoY)
Sidekick scaling (4x weekly active shops YoY; 12,000+ custom apps created in Q1 with Sidekick)
invisible complexity moat (checkout, payments, fraud, tax, shipping — LLMs do not bypass Shopify's checkout)
GMV scale as defensibility (two consecutive $100B+ GMV quarters; Shopify Payments 67% penetration)
summary: Shopify Q1 2026 is the most metrics-rich 'offensive' call in this batch: Harley Finkelstein presents AI not as a risk but as the single biggest tailwind for Shopify's core merchant thesis — 'there is simply no job that will be more accelerated by AI than entrepreneurship.' The Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) has now been joined by Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce, and Stripe, transforming it from a bilateral Google deal to a true industry standard. The 8x YoY growth in AI-driven traffic and 13x YoY growth in AI-powered orders are the strongest empirical proof-points in the batch that AI is additive to Shopify's GMV.

quotes.speaker: Harley Finkelstein
quotes.text: We're not approaching a new era anymore. We are already in it. In 2026, AI is now Shopify's native language. We bet early on AI and forced its adoption. It's embedded in everything we do, the products we build, the channels we power, the way every single person on the team operates. AI has become an exoskeleton for everyone at Shopify, giving them a virtual team of agents.

quotes.speaker: Harley Finkelstein
quotes.text: In the first quarter, AI-driven traffic to Shopify stores has grown 8x year-over-year, while orders from AI-powered searches have increased nearly 13x. Within this, new buyer orders are occurring at nearly twice the rate of other channels.

quotes.speaker: Harley Finkelstein
quotes.text: We are the only platform that enables discovery and selling inside ChatGPT, Copilot, and Google, all from one single system of record. Traffic from catalog-powered AI searches converts 2x more than traffic from general AI searches, where the agent is working from scraped or often outdated information from across the web. That is the value Shopify brings.

quotes.speaker: Harley Finkelstein
quotes.text: Last month, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce, and Stripe all joined the council, committing their expertise in internet scale transaction processing to build one Universal Commerce Protocol. The companies that power how the world shops are now building on one standard. Shopify is at the center of how commerce gets done in the age of AI agents.

quotes.speaker: Harley Finkelstein
quotes.text: There's always going to be some market confusion when we see a significant shift like we're seeing right now with the rise of AI. We've seen it before. I'm sure we'll see it again. Every single time the world gets more complex, Shopify gets more valuable. We absorb more of that complexity into our systems and become more valuable to merchants.

quotes.speaker: Harley Finkelstein
quotes.text: The number of weekly active shops using Sidekick in Q1 was up 4x year-over-year. We saw over 12,000 custom apps created in Q1 alone using Sidekick, and nearly half of all Shopify Flow generated in Q1 were built with Sidekick.

quotes.speaker: Harley Finkelstein
quotes.text: AI is certainly Shopify's native language. We bet early on it. We force its adoption, and now it is as reflexive inside our company as any company. There is simply no job that will be more accelerated by AI than entrepreneurship. In fact, it may be the most AI-safe job out there.

notes: EPS came in at -$0.45 vs. $0.32 estimated (Q1 2026), a large miss, driven by LVMH/luxury integrations and SBC-related charges. Despite this, management commentary was unambiguously bullish on AI. GMV hit $101B for the second consecutive quarter.

name: Automatic Data Processing (ADP)
whatIsRecord: Employee records, payroll, tax, benefits administration
description: The largest HCM/payroll system of record. Serves 1M+ clients globally.
themes: HCM as regulatory complexity amplifier (200+ HR compliance laws YoY, AI accelerates fragmentation)
payroll accuracy as irreducible human commitment ('payroll isn't a software function, it's a commitment')
AI-native data moat (1 in 6 U.S. workers, $3.3T moved, 77 years of workforce data)
ADP Assist agents at scale (payroll agent saves 30 min per payroll; Smart Actions reduces clicks 80%)
workforce displacement — no empirical evidence yet (Stanford Digital Economy Lab research cited)
regulatory AI governance moat (EU Pay Transparency Directive June 2026; 200+ laws YoY)
agentic ecosystem via ADP Marketplace (dedicated AI agent section with third-party partners)
summary: ADP Q3 FY2026 maintains its 'defensive' stance but the argument has become structurally stronger: Maria Black now frames AI as an amplifier of HCM complexity rather than a threat, citing 200+ new HR compliance laws enacted year-to-date and the EU Pay Transparency Directive as concrete examples of why clients need ADP more, not less, in the AI era. The ADP Assist agents are now quantified with real operational data (payroll agent saves 30 min/payroll, Smart Actions reduces clicks 80%), and the Stanford Digital Economy Lab partnership adds academic credibility to ADP's 'no empirical job displacement evidence' narrative. Critically, the 'Stanford research' framing replaces the CFO's anecdotal 'we're not seeing it in the data' language from Q1.

quotes.speaker: Maria Black
quotes.text: AI makes HCM more important, and we believe it unlocks tremendous value and opportunity for our industry that plays out in two ways. First, while AI excels at prediction and efficiency, it can't execute critical high-stakes HCM functions with the level of accuracy and consistency required. At the end of the day, payroll isn't a software function. It's a commitment to the people who showed up and did the work, and there is no room for error.

quotes.speaker: Maria Black
quotes.text: What differentiates ADP's approach is that our AI is built into the very core of how we orchestrate, govern, and execute HR and pay processes grounded in regulatory logic, operational data, and decades of expertise. This goes far beyond chatbots or surface layer automation that can enhance the user experience. It's about delivering real-world outcomes where accuracy and auditability are non-negotiable.

quotes.speaker: Maria Black
quotes.text: Our ADP Assist payroll agents have saved an average of 30 minutes per payroll. Our ADP Assist tax registration agents have helped businesses maintain compliance and avoid penalties and interest on late tax filings. Our Smart Actions search has reduced clicks and time spent by around 80% for common HR actions.

quotes.speaker: Maria Black
quotes.text: AI is changing both work and the workforce, and with our business grounded in all aspects of payroll and beyond, we are working on answers every single day. Our research with the Stanford Digital Economy Lab shows that AI is reshaping work at the task level. While this could lead to job displacement in certain task areas, we expect other new job categories to be created in this tech transformation.

quotes.speaker: Maria Black
quotes.text: So far this year, more than 200 HR-related compliance laws have been enacted in the U.S., including several governing the use of AI. This June, the EU Pay Transparency Directive will take effect. Employers continue to face increasingly complex and sometimes conflicting requirements across local, state, and federal jurisdictions. This is exactly where we thrive.

quotes.speaker: Maria Black
quotes.text: AI is only as good as the data it's built on, and ADP has the industry's strongest workforce data foundation built over nearly 77 years. We pay one in six workers in the U.S. and moved $3.3 trillion in the U.S. in fiscal 2025. We capture payroll, HR, and compliance events for more than 1.1 million clients and 42 million workers globally across roles, industries, and geographies, giving us incredible insights into the workforce and its emerging trends. This advantage will continue to compound.

quotes.speaker: Maria Black
quotes.text: Managing a workforce through disruption makes HCM more complex. We are not immune to shifting employment trends, but we are built for the world they represent.

notes: ADP announced 7% revenue growth and raised full-year guidance to 6-7% revenue growth and 10-11% adj. EPS growth. Record ES retention rate in Q3. ADP referenced Stanford Digital Economy Lab research as external validation of the 'no broad displacement yet' argument — a new institutional credibility mechanism versus Q1's anecdotal framing.

name: ServiceNow
whatIsRecord: IT assets, incidents, change requests, CMDB, workflows
description: The dominant ITSM SoR. Expanding into HR service delivery, CSM, security ops.
themes: AI Control Tower as enterprise governance OS
context engine as competitive moat (95B+ workflows trained)
agentic AI driving seat + consumption hybrid pricing (50% non-seat new business)
Autonomous Workforce product launch
SaaSpocalypse dismissal via 'rules and rails of business' framing
AI-native packaging — no sidecar AI
platform consolidation into IT/HR/CRM/security
summary: McDermott drops the defensive qualifier entirely this quarter, projecting pure confidence: 'There has never been a tailwind for ServiceNow like AI' and 'We would not trade positions with anyone.' The Control Tower narrative is now operationalized via Autonomous Workforce (teams of AI specialists), with 50% of net new business coming from non-seat-based pricing — a milestone that validates the consumption transition. The key moat argument shifted from governance to context compounding: 95 billion annual workflows trained, 7 trillion transactions processed, with the Context Engine learning from every decision ever made. The SaaSpocalypse counter-narrative is sharpest yet — McDermott draws a stark line between 'parlor tricks' and '22 years of excellence,' dismissing disruption fears as noise for a company he calls 'the AI-defining enterprise software company of the 21st century.'

quotes.speaker: Bill McDermott
quotes.text: There has never been a tailwind for ServiceNow like AI. Since Fred Luddy started the company, we've always focused our platform on the jobs our customers needed done.

quotes.speaker: Bill McDermott
quotes.text: Don't fall for the parlor trick that one touch button can replace 22 years of excellence. This is not a company that shrinks from challenges. It rises to every opportunity.

quotes.speaker: Bill McDermott
quotes.text: ServiceNow is the only enterprise AI platform that converts that chaos to control. We would not trade positions with anyone.

quotes.speaker: Bill McDermott
quotes.text: 50% of net new business now comes from a non-seat-based pricing model, including tokens and other assets such as infrastructure, hardware, and connectors. Our hybrid pricing model gives customers the best of both worlds.

quotes.speaker: Bill McDermott

summary: Descartes delivers its most expansive AI/SaaSpocalypse rebuttal yet in Q4 FY2026, with CEO Edward Ryan spending a full prepared-remarks section directly addressing 'AI could kill existing technology companies' — calling it a fundamental misunderstanding. Offensively, the GLN's proprietary logistics data is framed as 'rocket fuel for AI,' digital coworkers via MacroPoint are now in production across multiple use cases, and the acquisition of OrderMine brings AI-powered demand forecasting into the e-commerce pillar. Notably, Ryan revealed that product development velocity has collapsed from 'months and years' to 'weeks' using AI coding tools — a rare vibe coding acknowledgment by a SaaS CEO — while insisting this strengthens rather than threatens Descartes.

quotes.speaker: Edward Ryan
quotes.text: I've heard market commentators raise concerns about the impact of artificial intelligence technologies on the long-term prospects and terminal values of technology businesses. Specifically, that if AI can generate software code, then coding becomes commoditized and established technology companies are vulnerable to new entrant competitors or companies taking software coding in-house. In short, the headlines are, 'AI could kill existing technology companies.' I don't buy any of that. Those commentators are fundamentally misunderstanding the value technology companies bring to customers.

quotes.speaker: Edward Ryan
quotes.text: Descartes is a network services business. We run the Global Logistics Network. It's the world's largest connected community of supply chain and logistics participants, formed over more than 30 years. We use technology to help our customers solve complicated inter-enterprise supply chain and logistics problems on the GLN that require the cooperation of multiple parties and communities on the network. We're not an enterprise software company.

quotes.speaker: Edward Ryan
quotes.text: Descartes has the largest trove of real-time supply chain and logistics data in the world. We process billions of transactions a year. AI technologies are only as effective as the data they consume and only as relevant as the timeliness of the data they get. Most AI technologies are all trained on the same publicly available information on the internet. The real value is being able to train AI technologies using non-public information, which is exactly what information we have on our Global Logistics Network. Our Global Logistics Network data is rocket fuel for AI.

quotes.speaker: Edward Ryan
quotes.text: We think of an AI agent as a digital coworker trained to do a specific task. AI agents are excellent for reducing human workload by automating repetitive tasks. Historically, our services have been designed to only be used by human workers, often clicking on icons and entering data. However, that isn't the future. We're preparing our services to be used by either human or digital workers.

quotes.speaker: Edward Ryan
quotes.text: Our ability to come up with new ideas and roll them out is now weeks and months versus months and years. We're coming up with new ideas, and the ideas are coming so fast, and I'm shocked at how fast we're building these things, using off-the-shelf AI tools that we're adding to our network and using against our data. There's no coding involved. We're solving a problem for the customer.

quotes.speaker: Edward Ryan
quotes.text: Generative AI companies know the market is making a mistake by questioning the long-term prospects of technology companies. They're admitting that publicly, and they're running their own businesses by relying on specialist technology businesses rather than using their own AI tools to build an inferior quality enterprise system. The market's fears don't match reality.

quotes.speaker: Edward Ryan
quotes.text: ForecastMine is a strategic step forward in our e-commerce AI investments, accelerating our AI-powered forecasting and demand planning, particularly for e-commerce sellers using Shopify. We've got a huge pool of rich inventory, order, supplier, fulfillment, and returns data that ForecastMine can train on to help sellers do this.

notes: Stance unchanged at offensive-defensive; this is the second consecutive call (following Q1 2026) with an explicit SaaSpocalypse counter-narrative. Language has grown more assertive: 'rocket fuel for AI,' 'I don't buy any of that,' 'fool's errand.' Key new element: admission that AI coding tools now dramatically accelerate Descartes's own development — a double-edged signal the CEO explicitly positions as a Descartes advantage. The company articulated a clear shift from 'do-it-with-you' to 'do-it-for-you' with a forthcoming agent monetization model beyond traditional subscription and transaction fees, citing proprietary data ($1T+ in payments) as a structurally hard-to-replicate advantage.

quotes.speaker: René Lacerte
quotes.text: The tangible proof points we have seen rapidly deploying new agents to create more value for customers and driving greater productivity for employees have made it clear that this is no longer one priority among three. It is our number one priority.

quotes.speaker: René Lacerte
quotes.text: We have accelerated the adoption of our AI agents. To date, we have had well over 100,000 customers using our agents to improve their financial operations. From our touchless transactions agent to managing suppliers with our W-9 agent to our Invoice Coding Agent that has automated approximately 1.2 million invoices across over 9 million data fields, we are changing the game.

quotes.speaker: René Lacerte
quotes.text: We are aggressively moving our company to become AI native end-to-end and rapidly changing how we work. We are building AI so it will not just be a feature or function, but will serve as the fundamental core of our platform experience.

quotes.speaker: René Lacerte
quotes.text: Customers will not only be adopting software when they join BILL, they will be bringing on a team of expert agents that learn their financial back office and run it. They will autonomously identify which bills to pay, when to pay them, and how to route the cash, optimizing in real time against the business' actual financial position.

quotes.speaker: René Lacerte
quotes.text: Our platform has moved over $1 trillion in payments and processed over 1 billion financial documents. This makes us a data company. We have unique data assets in the B2B payments landscape derived from the behaviors and context generated by hundreds of millions of B2B transactions. This proprietary data set is structurally hard to replicate, creating a durable compounding advantage for our AI solutions.

quotes.speaker: René Lacerte
quotes.text: We enforce the right way to handle money, which involves domain-specific guardrails, compliance logic, operational controls, and proprietary context that generic AI does not have.

quotes.speaker: René Lacerte
quotes.text: It's not just gonna be subscription and transaction revenue. As we move from task-based kind of capabilities to jobs and roles, there will be opportunities to kind of monetize those agents differently than we've seen before.

quotes.speaker: René Lacerte
quotes.text: The summary is that building in an AI world where the distance and time between ideation and execution is shrinking rapidly and compressing requires a different organizational structure. We have to drive focus and clarity across the organization at a speed that we haven't had to do in the past.

notes: Stance escalated from offensive-defensive to offensive. 30% RIF explicitly framed as AI-native restructuring. New agent monetization model teased beyond subscription/transaction. Pay For You agent processing tens of thousands of fully autonomous card transactions.

quotes.speaker: Eric Clark
quotes.text: Because we build all these agents directly into the Active® Platform, our customers don't need to implement costly and complex external data lakes to make them work. Our unified cloud-native API-first architecture enables us to deploy agents with almost no configuration or additional upfront effort, embedding AI agents directly into the workflow. No data lakes, no latency, deployed in minutes, not months, creating value for our customers in real time.

quotes.speaker: Eric Clark
quotes.text: Core to our agentic AI philosophy is the concept of embedding both interactive and autonomous agents directly within the workflows of our key users. Rather than wave planners and shipping supervisors trying to incorporate standalone, disconnected AI platforms, our Active® Agents meet them where they live all day. By making AI ever present and highly available, our AI capabilities feel natural. They're steeped in both domain expertise and real-time operational data, always making suggestions and ready to take action autonomously.

quotes.speaker: Eric Clark
quotes.text: In some of the early conversations we've had around moving from pilot to subscription, there have been customers that have justified the entire ROI just by reduction in overtime.

quotes.speaker: Eric Clark
quotes.text: This concept that's been kicked around in the AI space here recently about headless, we're set up for headless. Our user interface can be the screens that we build, or our user interface can be an AI agent.

quotes.speaker: Eric Clark
quotes.text: We expect this to continue to scale as we go throughout each quarter, and I think we'll have more clarity on what that means as we go throughout each quarter. quotes.speaker: Eric Clark
quotes.text: This services team that we have here at Manhattan has become a massive advantage for us because we are skilling and tooling teams of forward deployed engineers that are made up of people from R&D and services engineers that can very quickly get these agents active for our customers.

quotes.speaker: Eric Clark
quotes.text: When you're using AI and automation, you don't want to sell services by the hour. You want to sell it by the outcome.

notes: Stance unchanged at offensive. First full quarter of agent availability. Q1 2026 cloud revenue +24% YoY. FDE team growing: ~120 net adds, ~70 pending. Largest ever OMS deal closed. Momentum user conference (Las Vegas) featuring Agent Boot Camp coming in May 2026.

quotes.speaker: Matt Hawkins

quotes.speaker: Matt Hawkins
quotes.text: AI-powered capabilities drove roughly 40% of new bookings in Q1, and our clients leaned into the platform for prevention, automation, and visibility rather than downstream rework.

quotes.speaker: Matt Hawkins

quotes.speaker: Matt Hawkins
quotes.text: Providers are reducing recoupment reconciliation time by over 80%, and one early adopter health system matched $32 million in revenue risk, work equivalent to approximately 13 full-time employees.

quotes.speaker: Matt Hawkins
quotes.text: We view AI as a tailwind and as the biggest opportunity in our lifetime.

quotes.speaker: Matt Hawkins

quotes.speaker: Sandeep Sahai (CEO)
quotes.text: Generative AI leadership rests on three foundational pillars which are very difficult for our competitors to replicate without many years of investment. quotes.speaker: Sandeep Sahai (CEO)
quotes.text: The breadth of data on our platform is extensive. We connect to approximately 4,000 data sources. quotes.speaker: Sandeep Sahai (CEO)

quotes.speaker: Sandeep Sahai (CEO)
quotes.text: Our GenAI investments are producing meaningful internal efficiencies, driving Non-GAAP gross margin to a record 79.2%. We embraced the technology early in 2023, used it to drive very meaningful gross margin improvements and have brought this technology to our clients.

summary: QTWO upgraded its AI posture in Q1 2026 from defensive to defensive-offensive by announcing two concrete AI products — Q2 Code (AI-assisted development for FIs) and AI-driven fraud prevention (account takeover detection) — while reinforcing its 'system of context' thesis. Matt Flake noted that customers are entirely reliant on Q2 for AI strategy and direction, signaling strong platform lock-in. Management introduced a hybrid pricing model (subscription base + credit/token overages) for AI products and acknowledged agentic AI as the next frontier, while being explicit that trust, compliance, and security are prerequisites that validate Q2's incumbency advantage.

quotes.speaker: Matt Flake
quotes.text: While the core processor is the transactional system of record, Q2 sits in the flow of every digital interaction, seeing every login, transaction, alert, message, and user decision. That gives us the context of behavior, not just ledger entries. We believe that's the kind of banking-specific context AI needs to be useful, and it's a meaningful differentiator for us.

quotes.speaker: Matt Flake
quotes.text: As AI lowers the cost of generating insights and writing code, we believe the value shifts towards platforms that can apply those insights in a trusted, compliant, and operationally sound way. That's where we believe the platform we've been building gives us a real advantage.

quotes.speaker: Matt Flake
quotes.text: Looking ahead, AI is moving toward more agentic models where systems take action on behalf of users. In financial services, that will require trust, transparency, and control. The platforms that win will combine context, execution, and compliance. We believe that Q2 is uniquely positioned to be one of them.

quotes.speaker: Matt Flake
quotes.text: It's the latter. I haven't seen anybody taking their own AI initiative and doing it on their own. They're partnering with us, learning from us, and we're trying to learn the problems they want to solve and build products to solve them.

quotes.speaker: Matt Flake
quotes.text: Right now I would say most of the customers are looking for AI tools that can help them run the bank as opposed to change the bank. Our Q2 Assistant, Q2 Code are in those areas. Personalization, cross-selling products, understanding customers, and what their next needs are definitely part of the roadmap.

quotes.speaker: Jonathan Price
quotes.text: Q2 Code — this is a discreetly monetizable product SKU. This shouldn't be confused with AI features built into an existing product. We're in the early adopter phase, working with beta customers around pricing models and building an idea of what monetization and revenue models could look like in the long run.

quotes.speaker: Jonathan Price
quotes.text: What we'll call is a credit, which includes underlying token utilization, but other infrastructure and the value prop that we're delivering through that product platform. That's sort of where it sits today as a vision and a target of a hybrid model — a subscription fee with a lot of that value bundled in a base size, then the excess comes from over that amount, with caps to ensure we don't go upside down in the interim.

notes: Stance shifted from defensive to defensive-offensive. Q1 2026 revenue +14% YoY to $216.5M, record EBITDA margin of 27.7% (+630bps YoY). Best-ever Q1 bookings including largest fraud deal in company history. Cloud migration completed in Jan 2026 driving gross margin step-up to 62.1%.

In just 4-5 weeks of limited availability, Celeste drove 15%+ of net new bookings and generated outsized demand signals (3x engagement on content, 9-min average visit time, 65%+ above-goal sales meetings in April). Major AI players — Microsoft, Harvey, and Anthropic — publicly validated the platform at Amplify. John Hall articulated a new TAM expansion thesis: as AI automates knowledge work, Intapp can capture a share of personnel budgets beyond software, with consumption-based pricing tied to activity volume (matters, deals, engagements). An Am Law 100 firm chose Intapp over a 'well-funded AI startup' in the quarter.

quotes.speaker: John Hall
quotes.text: Celeste delivers expert agents directly into the workflows that drive firm performance, business origination, deal and asset management, business intake and compliance, and revenue management. Built for firms, not adapted from tools built for everyone else.

quotes.speaker: John Hall
quotes.text: As AI automates knowledge work inside firms, Intapp can move beyond competing for software budgets and capture a larger share of overall personnel budgets, pricing for the value that expert agents create and for the volume of activity flowing through the platform. Matters opened, deals managed, engagements resourced, compliance actions approved.

quotes.speaker: John Hall
quotes.text: An Am Law 100 firm chose Intapp Time for its trusted AI capabilities after a well-funded AI startup competitor fell short of what their firm actually required. This is a pattern in the market.

quotes.speaker: John Hall
quotes.text: What's been really interesting to hear back from the prospects is they've really struggled with some of the first-generation tools in exactly the areas that we designed Celeste to address. MCP is an important technology architecture for this generation, but it is revealing and creating a lot of new repositories of business information that are essentially ungoverned by the firm's professional compliance requirements. What we've done with the Celeste architecture is exactly what addresses this core point.

quotes.speaker: John Hall
quotes.text: The firms are creating a second budget for AI solutions specifically, which we're now able to sell into. We're looking increasingly at the conversations with firms about their personnel budget, because part of the promise of the agentic strategy is can you offset some of your hiring in the future with agents rather than additional headcount as your firm continues to scale?

quotes.speaker: John Hall
quotes.text: We provide the professional compliance capability and the agentic orchestration for all of those across multiple solution types and multiple models at the same time. People really like that design.

quotes.speaker: John Hall
quotes.text: Many of these systems encourage the users to drag documents and information into them so they can do really exciting analysis. What's happening is larger and larger pools of ungoverned information are being formed inside these firms as they try these first-generation AI tools.

quotes.speaker: David Morton
quotes.text: Just a few months removed from our Celeste product announcement, over 15% of net new bookings in the quarter was driven by our Celeste AI solutions, including early monetization from firm AI pilots. We're seeing strong enterprise adoption across land, expand, and vertical motions, reinforcing AI as a durable driver of cloud growth.

notes: Massive stance shift from defensive to offensive. Cloud ARR +31% YoY to $459M. 123% Cloud NRR. Record free cash flow of $63.4M. Celeste in limited availability only (4-5 weeks of Q3), general availability ahead. quotes.speaker: Raul Villar Jr. (CEO)
quotes.text: The assistant is a next step in our AI evolution as we continue to drive efficiency and effectiveness so customers can focus on higher value work. quotes.speaker: Adam Ante (CFO)
quotes.text: It's really about enabling efficiency and enabling them to be able to navigate workflows more rapidly, navigate their own policies internally, as well as all the other areas that we've been building into the platform over the last couple of years. All that continues. As we think about how to monetize this and really where this can go, we think that this sort of usability and the ability to navigate is really what we'll continue to invest in. So I think you'll see more and more functionality and capability that will come through this Paycor Assistant and how people engage in our software. From a revenue perspective, I think it's still a little bit early, but we do want to, we do see this as a monetization opportunity with some of the more advanced AI solutions like this assistant. quotes.speaker: Adam Ante (CFO)
quotes.text: A lot of the data investments that we've made and the structure that we've been able to utilize to enable a lot of the AI capabilities, we've been making the data investments for a long time. So how do we leverage AI to make the product more usable for clients, for employees, for associates? And we're starting really with that mobile experience.

quotes.speaker: Adam Ante (CFO)
quotes.text: Yeah. I mean, we started with pilots, and the pilot feedback is great. I mean, it's still really early days, but the pilot feedback is great. People are excited about it. I mean, I think that there's high expectations for how you engage with LLM models with some really great consumer-like applications out there. We have some ideas about it, but we're not locked in on anything with regards to the monetization just yet.

quotes.speaker: Raul Villar Jr. (CEO)

We're going to continue to open the platform, and we want to continue to make it easier for our clients to connect their data to all the tools they want to use.

quotes.speaker: Sean Desmond
quotes.text: With over 170 customers of all sizes, including global, enterprise, regional, and community banks and credit unions having already purchased AI intelligence units as of the end of fiscal 2026, we believe nCino is rapidly becoming the de facto AI platform for financial institutions across the globe.

quotes.speaker: Sean Desmond
quotes.text: Because of this, we believe AI agents actually increase the value of our underlying platform and system of record. An agent can't operate in a vacuum. It needs trusted data, industry context, and guardrails, and it needs to be traceable and auditable. The platform that connects the user to the data and records the actions taken becomes the natural home for these AI-driven experiences. nCino is that platform.

quotes.speaker: Sean Desmond
quotes.text: Banking Advisor usage up over 25 times in March compared to usage in October. Customers are not just buying AI access, they're using it, and we can see that directly in the increasing consumption of intelligence units on our platform.

quotes.speaker: Sean Desmond
quotes.text: We strongly believe that proprietary, domain-specific, real-world data is the most valuable asset in an AI economy, and no other company has the data nCino has. That data moat compounds with every customer we add and every line of business we expand into.

quotes.speaker: Sean Desmond
quotes.text: While other companies are scrambling to deliver user experiences overnight with no foundation of data, we actually continue to build on 14 years of buildup. We believe our data moat is unparalleled and unique and nobody else has the type of contextual view on how capital flows through workflows in financial institutions.

quotes.speaker: Sean Desmond
quotes.text: In some cases, we're seeing months to days and days to minutes. We plan on highlighting at nSight some direct outcomes, e.g., sharing their experiences on leveraging those units. There's a direct correlation between the outcomes our customers are getting and the intelligence units they're drawing down on across the spectrum of Banking Advisor.

quotes.speaker: Owen Ryan
quotes.text: At our AI investor session in March, we shared our technology vision in detail and made our case for why BlackLine is positioned to be the trusted governance and control layer for CFOs deploying AI across their financial operations.
quotes.context: Prepared remarks — positioning as AI governance layer

quotes.speaker: Owen Ryan
quotes.text: As an enterprise deploys AI agents across their business in procurement, sales operations, accounts payable, they are creating new uncontrolled financial touch points that need to be governed. Every one of those AI-generated transactions eventually hits the general ledger. Every one must be reconciled, validated, and audited. For a CFO who personally attests to the accuracy of financial statements, that is a responsibility that requires a trusted platform.
quotes.context: Prepared remarks — Agentic Financial Operations market thesis

quotes.speaker: Owen Ryan
quotes.text: Over 2/3 of our customers are now actively using these tools, a 285% increase in adoption quarter-over-quarter. In Q1 alone, unique users grew 68% and total usage grew 183%. What this tells us is that AI is moving beyond experimentation for our customers and into their day-to-day workflows.
quotes.context: Prepared remarks — AI adoption milestone

quotes.speaker: Owen Ryan
quotes.text: Verity Prepare, our AI-powered reconciliation agent, is now available to customers and is deployed with several mega enterprise customers. The validated outcomes customers are seeing are significant. Over 90% reduction in reconciliation processing time.
quotes.context: Prepared remarks — Verity Prepare outcomes

quotes.speaker: Owen Ryan
quotes.text: In one early adopter scenario, our AI agent completed collections outreach activities in under 30 minutes that would have taken a human team approximately 45 hours. That kind of efficiency gain, freeing collection teams to focus on high-value accounts and complex disputes, is exactly what is driving the demand we are seeing.
quotes.context: Prepared remarks — Verity Collect efficiency data

quotes.speaker: Owen Ryan
quotes.text: Every action an AI agent takes within BlackLine leaves a digital footprint identical to a human user, full chain of thought, immutable audit trails, embedded controls. This is what CFOs demand, what audit committees rely upon, and what auditors require.
quotes.context: Prepared remarks — audit trail as moat

quotes.speaker: Owen Ryan
quotes.text: The time from idea to production has decreased 22% versus last year. We are shipping capabilities faster, with fewer resources, at a higher quality. This is a structural improvement in R&D productivity that we expect to compound over time.
quotes.context: Prepared remarks — internal AI engineering velocity

quotes.speaker: Owen Ryan
quotes.text: Our customers are not just looking to buy AI for the sake of AI. For our customer base, it's about being part of the digital financial transformation journey that happens to have more power being provided because of AI. People are just not buying the whipped cream without wanting the cake.

summary: Zuora (last public call before its February 2025 take-private) took a uniquely meta-offensive stance: rather than worrying about AI disrupting their own SaaS model, they positioned their monetization platform as the infrastructure layer that enables other SaaS companies to implement AI-driven consumption billing. Advanced Consumption Billing was their fastest-growing product, driven directly by the SaaS industry's shift to usage-based AI pricing. Acquisitions of Togai (metering) and Sub(x) (AI RL paywalls) accelerated this vision of 'Total Monetization' — blending subscriptions, consumption, and outcome-based pricing.

quotes.speaker: Tien Tzuo (CEO)
quotes.text: Over time, we believe that companies will need to be able to monetize with any business model, and this is what we mean by Total Monetization. And we're seeing this concept really resonate. Those of you who joined us at Subscribed Live in the Bay Area in June saw these conversations are happening with our customers and prospects. Companies are coming to us and saying, 'You captured the essence of what we're trying to do.' And so this vision is fueling our innovation. Three quick examples from the quarter. First, our Advanced Consumption Billing vision. In Q2, Advanced Consumption Billing was one of our fastest-growing products, in part driven by the rollout and monetization of AI features that you are seeing from almost all the technology vendors.

quotes.speaker: Tien Tzuo (CEO)
quotes.text: The acquisition we announced in Q1 and closed in Q2, giving us some of the most advanced metering and rating technology in the marketplace today. Second, in Q2, we also announced the acquisition of Sub(x) to add new AI capabilities that will strengthen our Zephr products, offering media companies an advanced AI-powered paywall solution. Through Reinforcement Learning, Sub(x) helps media companies put the right offer in front of the right customer, maximizing subscriber acquisition and conversion, all without manual testing and experimentation.

quotes.speaker: Tien Tzuo (CEO)
quotes.text: If a company is trying to collect a payment and that payment fails, our Smart Retry in Zuora Payments analyzes over 15 transaction characteristics, such as the account monthly recurring revenue, the currency, the payment gateway, to automatically retry the failed payment at the most optimal time. We're continuing to make the AI technology that powers Smart Retry more and more advanced, and in Q2 alone, we helped our customers recover over $120 million in lost revenue with the Smart Retry capability. That's an increase of over 40% year-over-year.

quotes.speaker: Tien Tzuo (CEO)
quotes.text: The way I look at total monetization, and I appreciate the question, Adam, is it really allows us to continue the journey we've been on. In many ways, you can think of it almost as an act two, where the first phase of the company was really offering, you know, billing to companies that were pure subscription businesses... And total monetization is to say, look, now that subscription businesses and recurring revenue models are becoming more prevalent, companies are really looking to be much more sophisticated and blend these different business models together. So it's not just about subscriptions, it's about consumption, it's about one-time fees, it's about outcome-based fees, it's about really mixing all these things and customizing the right business model and the right pricing model for the customer.

quotes.speaker: Tien Tzuo (CEO)
quotes.text: We're seeing, you know, maybe you call these paywall 3.0 strategies that are, you know, not a surprise, AI-driven, right? That says, we don't want static scores, right? We want something that's dynamic, we want something that's changing, we want something that can look at the data. Given where AI is and technology is, there's no reason they can't do that. And so we've doubled down on our Zephr investment with Sub(x), which really gives it an AI-driven decision tree, right? Using, you know, an AI technique called reinforcement learning to figure out in real time, hey, this subscriber coming to your newspaper site, your app, what do you wanna do? Do you want to let them look at the article? Do you want to put an offer in front of them?

quotes.speaker: Todd McElhatton (President)
quotes.text: Capturing it, ingesting it, translating that, transforming it, and ultimately applying a price to it, right? That's what we mean by metering and rating, and that's the capability that Togai really, you know, gave us a two-year head start in terms of what we can do just basically by ourselves. So, we're still selling Advanced Consumption Billing like we did before, but I think the vision of where that product is going is now, you know, significantly stronger, you know, multiple times better, and it's getting, you know, really positive traction when we talk to our customers and prospects about it.
